entries.title: Proverbs 6:1
segments:
Stricken thy hand; it was thus that a person pledged himself to be responsible for the debt of another. 
 
He who easily allows himself to become surety for others, is likely to become the prey of weak or designing men, who make false representations of their circumstances.  To make suretyship lawful and proper, we must be fully able to meet the sum pledged without injury to others.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:3
segments: Into the hand of thy friend; into his power.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:11
segments:
One that travelleth; a traveller that comes unexpectedly, as an enemy or assailant. 
 
Indolent procrastination is the parent of poverty and misery in things temporal and spiritual.  The divine law is, that wealth of every kind comes by toil.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:12
segments:
vv 12-15. 
 
These verses describe a cunning deceiver, who accomplishes his mischievous plans by hidden artifices. 
 
  Winketh--speaketh--teacheth; the secret signs which he gives to his accomplices.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:15
segments: The man who relies for success upon crooked and deceitful practices, is alike odious to God and man, and his end will be remediless ruin.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:16
segments: Six things--yea, seven; it is a frequent custom of the Hebrew writers, in making enumerations, to begin with one less than the whole number.

God estimates men, not from their outward circumstances, but from their character.  All whose hearts and lives are defiled with wicked practices are abominable in his sight, however high their reputation among men.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:23
segments: Are the way of life; they guide men into the way of life.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:27
segments: The penalty of sin is as certain as the laws of nature, and far more terrible in its power.  The youth who enters upon a course of impurity, throws himself into a consuming fire, which will destroy both soul and body.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:30
segments: Despise; generally interpreted to mean, to overlook, to connive at. But we may retain the ordinary meaning of the word.  Though men feel the necessity of punishing a thief who has stolen to satisfy his hunger, yet they do not look upon him with such contempt and abhorrence as upon the adulterer.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:32
segments: He that doeth it destroyeth his own soul; more literally, The destroyer of his own soul, he will do it; as much as to say, The man who is bent on ruining himself, he will commit this sin.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:34
segments: The rage of a man; in an emphatic sense, jealousy excites his fiercest rage.
